nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group. A set $C$ of subgroups of $G$ is a partition of $G$ when every member of $C$ is a proper subgroup of $G$, every element of $G$ lies in some member of $C$, and any two distinct members of $C$ intersect in the trivial subgroup. The members of $C$ are called its components.
nodes.title: Partition of a group

nodes.summary: For every prime $p$, every finite $p$-group $G$ and every partition $C$ of $G$ (a set of proper subgroups of $G$ whose union is $G$ and any two distinct members of which intersect in the trivial subgroup), some member $H$ of $C$ is abelian, that is, $xy = yx$ for all $x, y \in H$.
nodes.title: Every partition of a finite $p$-group has an abelian component

nodes.summary: The statement that for every prime $p$, every finite $p$-group $G$ and every partition $C$ of $G$ (a set of proper subgroups of $G$ whose union is $G$ and any two distinct members of which intersect in the trivial subgroup), some member $H$ of $C$ is abelian, that is, $xy = yx$ for all $x, y \in H$.
nodes.title: Berkovich's question on abelian components of partitions

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
